the Nones noun

the fifth or seventh day of the Roman month

also Nones

classical

Varro, LL 6.28 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 14.20: aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē
Traupman 78–79

Nōnae, Nōnārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

the Nones, the 5th of the month (the 7th in March, May, July and October)

The ninth day before the Ides, counting both ends (nōnus; Varro, LL 6.28, in Lewis & Short). The month’s adjective agrees with it: Nōnae Februāriae, 5 February; Nōnīs Mārtiīs, on 7 March. The days before are counted back to it: prīdiē Nōnās Jānuāriās, 4 January; ante diem tertium Nōnās Majās, 5 May.

Examples

  • in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē

    we expect to reach the house at Tusculum on the Nones (of October, the 7th) or the day afterCic. Fam. 14.20

  • Latīnae fēriae fuēre ante diem tertium Nōnās Majās

    the Latin Festival was held on 5 May, the third day before the NonesLiv. 41.16.1

See also the Kalends, the Ides, month, calendar.
